sourceIssues.reason: As printed, c is an isomorphism between a module over Ŵ(A_G̃/a_G̃) and one over Ŵ(A_G̃), which does not typecheck. The comparison is the one modulo a_G̃, as the following Proposition 3.2.7 uses ("a section of T which is constant mod a_E"). The ideal is defined from the maximal ideal m_{A_G̃} just introduced; "A_E" is a label slip. Noted by the extraction (items D07, D09).

review.reason: Checked at p.23 of arXiv 2103.09945v2 (SHA-256 62d26eb9…34c8, the version named): the text defines the maximal ideal m_{A_G̃} of A_G̃ and then sets a_G̃ := m²_{A_E} + π_E A_E, with an undefined A_E; the definition must use A_G̃. In c : Ũ_1 ⊗_{Z̆_p} Ŵ(A_G̃/a_G̃) ≅ M̃_1 ⊗_{Ŵ(A)} Ŵ(A_G̃), the two sides are modules over different rings, and the very-good condition c(s_{α,0} ⊗ 1) = s_{α,0} ⊗ 1 is a statement over A_G̃/a_G̃. So both sides are base-changed to Ŵ(A_G̃/a_G̃), as the correction says.

sourceIssues.reason: The proof continues: "In particular G satisfies the first assumption in Lemma 4.2.4 below. Thus by that lemma …". Lemma 4.2.4 assumes "X_*(G^ab)_I is torsion-free". Moreover G^ab contains the similitude quotient, so X_*(G^ab)_I has positive rank and cannot be a torsion group. The justification given ("our assumptions imply that G^ad_2 does not have a simple factor of the form Res_{F/Q_p} PGL_m(D) …") is the torsion-freeness criterion. Checked on the page image by the extraction. Noted by the extraction (item S19).

sourceIssues.reason: ṫ_λ lifts the translation t_λ of the Iwahori–Weyl group, and for λ ≠ 0 it is not in the positive loop group G(F_q[[t]]). The proof works with G(k[[t]]) ∩ ṫ_λ G(k[[t]]) ṫ_λ^{−1} ⊂ G(k((t))). The application in the proof of Proposition 5.2.3 chooses "the lift ṫ_λ ∈ G(F_q((t)))". Noted by the extraction (item C08).

review.reason: Checked at p.52: ṫ_λ lifts the translation t^λ and lies in the loop group G(F_q((t))); if it lay in G(F_q[[t]]) it would be in L^+G and the orbit would be that of the base point. The proof uses only that ṫ_λ is F_q-rational, to get σ_q(ṫ_λ) = ṫ_λ and then σ_q(h) = hk before Lang's theorem. That is the hypothesis ṫ_λ ∈ G(F_q((t))).
